utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Since this was a very lengthy re-examination by the Prosecution, if there are any questions to the content of this redirect to be fair to both parties, I would like to ask Mr. Tolimir from the redirect if there arose any additional questions from your side?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. There are a lot of such questions. I'll try and put only those that are relevant to send the witness home because he has stayed even longer than necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I hope that should be the case every time to put only those who are relevant. It is not necessary to put irrelevant questions to any witness. Just in answer to your remark.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I did not mean relevancy or irrelevancy when it comes to the questions. I meant the time that is left to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I believe that General Tolimir intends to use up the rest of the time that we have, and we have another witness which I'd like to get permission to release at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed. We have not enough time left today to commence with another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Can the document stay in e-court. Let's start with last things first in order to speed things along.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, based on the documents that you see in front of you, can you tell me whether you issued tasks to all the members of the staff which you can see here in the structure?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You didn't. Okay. Were you in a position to issue tasks to the member of staff for the "asanacija" who is the 7th in order here?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So would that be somebody else who would have issued him orders from the civilian protection side or would it have been the president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who it would have been. I only know that I was not the one who issued orders to him. I don't know whether somebody else ordered him, whether the chief of the Ministry of Defence or somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us whether you had the right to expect documents of the Ministry of Defence which are marked as military secrets or something else, or was it only the person who worked within the structure of the Ministry of Defence who could do that?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have an insight into those documents. They are not a municipality body. They were the body of the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us when the president of municipality became the commissioner, as you said it during the cross-examination, was his position vacant and were his authorities transferred on to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you have confused some things. Deronjic was never the head of the municipality. The head of the municipality was Ljubisa Simic and he remained in that position all the time. And Miroslav Deronjic was the commissioner. He was the president of the local SDS as well as of the regional board of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You are right, I got mixed up. So before you, if somebody was given a task from the ministry in the municipality, would it have been the president or you, who would it have been?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it would have been both.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about military tasks, was the civilian body of power in a position to receive any tasks from the military in this particular situation?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not superior to us, to the civilian authorities. The military had nothing whatsoever to do with the civilian authorities, they were not our superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was the principal of command responsibility applied in the municipal structures? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, could you please rephrase or be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: When it comes to the civilian bodies of power, do they -- did they fall under the criteria that were applied to the military bodies of authorities, for example, command responsibility?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not fall under those. The Executive Board was answerable to the Assembly of the municipality of Bratunac because throughout the war the civilian authorities were functioning in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecutor asked you whether you removed the dead bodies, if you heard that there were dead bodies strewn around, was that part of your competencies?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not the one who removed them. I don't know under whose orders the civilian protection did that as well as the utility company. They received orders and they can tell you who from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: If there were any bodies on the street in town, was the president of the municipality in charge of removing that or was it the case that military bodies and civilian bodies came first to inspect, and after all the procedures was followed, the president of the municipality would issue an order for the bodies to be removed? It would not be him who would remove them?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there was a procedure in place. A human body is not a dead cat in the street. Of course doctors should be involved, the police should be involved, and after that the civilian protection and utility company that looks after the cleanliness of a town.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether the civilian bodies or the bodies of the Ministry of Defence, like, for example the civilian protection, would dare enter a combat area without an invitation on the part of the commander of the military in charge -- military unit or district to remove dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose not. You can't enter a combat area at your own will. You can do it only upon somebody's invitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 49, lines from 1 through 11, the Prosecutor asked you about a certain man, Ibro. Let's not mention his family name. I don't know whether we were in private or open session. I'm hurrying because I want to send you home. Do you remember what he asked you?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question would be this: Was it within your purview to follow that gentleman's free will and let him go where he wanted or was it within somebody else's purview?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was within somebody else's purview, and it was according to his expressed wish, the wish that he stated himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. After the meeting, did you have any contacts with the aforementioned gentleman?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ibro?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. At the meeting at Fontana, were there representatives of the Red Cross there?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody was there on behalf of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the recording that the Prosecution showed you, did you recognise anybody from the Red Cross at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you notice -- that wrote the minutes, did you notice he mentioned them as having been there?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that in the report, but they were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is it possible that that was a collective report for the entire day because it mentions that meeting at 8.00, the 10.00 meeting, about the appointment of police officers, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say so. There are many items of the agenda which were not all dealt with at the 8.00 and 10.00 meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In one point it says current -- the present tense is used, in another the future tense and then the past tense, is that an indicative, does it indicate that that was the collective report for the entire day? Did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice the 1500. If that report was written up at 1500 hours, then -- well, beforehand there was 8.00 and 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have document 003937. That's the ERN number. Could we have that on the left-hand side, and the right-hand side Y003-9038, on the right-hand side, that is so that we can compare are the two. That is Prosecution number -- I apologise, I wrote this up incorrectly. I skipped a page. I do apologise. I'm in a rush, I'm speaking off the cuff and I didn't realise that there was this other page in front of me. Prosecution showed a document here as 00 -- P00416. And the exhibit 65 ter was on page 14, line 24. So could we see in e-court this document under seal, 65 ter P00416. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It can't be the right page to that document. It should be removed from the screen, please. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be removed because it's a secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think I'll just withdraw what I was going to say, I think we are fine as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I hope it was not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I do apologise. I meant P00752. That's a document of the centre of security services from Zvornik from the 12th. Let us see the original and the copy. Let's see the original on one side and then the copy on the other side. Could the witness please see it in a language he understands and then can the Trial Chamber see it in English. Thank you. 65 ter 752. Thank you. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that document was admitted, P1259A and B. These may be the two documents General Tolimir is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you to Mr. Vanderpuye. I'm speaking about this document of the chief of the Zvornik MUP. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see the document now. Could the witness please have a look at paragraph 4. Can he read or see anything in paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Consultations are underway to appoint the chief of the Srebrenica" --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, that will do. That's it. The Prosecutor asked you whether you and the Muslims discussed that at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, and I apologise to the interpreters. Does this indicate the fact that what happened at 8.00 and what is underway, that this was written up as a document, a comprehensive document for the entire day as seen by the gentleman who wrote up the document?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the way it looks on the basis of this paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does this document show that as for the knowledge that he had on that entire day he put that into these paragraph that preceded activities? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is his daily report to the ministry, Ministry of Security, the office of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 46 of today's transcript, line 11, you said: "It was my understanding that they would be checking those who stay on in Srebrenica." When the Prosecutor asked you what Mladic meant by saying that those who remained would be prosecuted, as you had put it. My question is: Is a prosecution a complex action or is it just a check based on an interview with a suspect?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certainly a complex action.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Sorry. On page 46, line 22, the Prosecutor asked you how you interpret what Mladic said when he asked everyone what to do with the Muslims and when it was said that the Muslims could survive or disappear. In this sentence, the Muslims could survive or disappear, are both referred to? What was your understanding, did that depend on Mladic or the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that it depended on the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask a short question just to clarify. We heard that you took part in the Hotel Fontana meeting at that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving any interpretation again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving any interpretation either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I put this question once again. Did you attend the Hotel Fontana meeting that day at 10.00?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Dragomir Vasic present at this meeting too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The Prosecutor, on page 50, line 5, asked you whether you passed by the Vuk Karadzic school and whether you had heard that there were corpses there and whether you removed those corpses. My question is: Is the president of the municipality responsible for removing corpses from public areas in town, since you said that you had not seen that, would he have to inform the appropriate authorities in the municipality who are supposed to establish what the situation is?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just passed by the school. I did not enter the school because in front of the school building I saw a policeman, and I said to him what I had said, namely to take care of Resid.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The president of the Executive Board, can he, without the agreement of the army and police, remove corpses or perhaps even protect them as an ordinary soldier could be asked to do? Could you have done that on the basis of your position?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. A question was put to you here about the brothers of the late Resid when he said that a shell had fallen and that he had not heard of them since.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is it possible that when the area was being mopped up, when the -- and after the shell had fallen there, perhaps were their bodies brought to the grave that the Prosecutor referred to?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even Resid didn't know what happened with his brother and his relative. This was the last time he saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you know anything about these two men then?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not. And I didn't really make an effort or express any interest or did I have any possibility of finding out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: As we are looking at this document here, Mr. Ilic said here that the Muslims were withdrawing towards Srebrenica -- Suceska, rather, from Potocari from the place where he attended the meeting. Can one see Suceska and how far away is that in terms of kilometres? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot see it from there and it must be about 15 kilometres away from Potocari in this hilly mountainous area. That's where Suceska is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you mentioned a certain name on page 75, line 25. I think you misspoke. You were referring to Mr. Vasic and not to Mr. Ilic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. You are right. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does that indicate the fact that the gentleman who we mentioned just now could have written this report only on the basis of the reports that were coming in from the field because this area cannot be seen from Potocari and from the place where he was in Bratunac, Potocari at the meeting and so on? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know on the basis of which information Vasic wrote this up. However, he certainly could not have seen that. He knows what his knowledge was when he wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know out in the field in the broader area of Zvornik, who could have issued an order for mopping up the area, the theatre of war, civilian or military organs?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was only the military organs that could have done that. That was their area of responsibility and war operations were still underway, so it was dangerous and it would have been dangerous for civilians to go there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we have to redact page 77, lines 5 to 9. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't know whether the transcript reflects the witness's last answer. If that is the case, I'm not going to repeat my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It does. Carry on with your next question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: During the re-examination you had several questions put to you about Kravica and the attack that took place there, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you have any powers in Kravica and in relation to the population of Kravica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in relation to the civilian population in Kravica that was not in the war operation zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. This attack that was launched by the Muslims, was it launched in depth in the territory and how many kilometres away was that from the front line?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in depth in the territory, it must be about 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the Muslims stay in that territory, or after having inflicting these losses, after having killed soldiers and civilians, did they return to the territory that they controlled?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After having looted and torched, they went back to their territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did that look like sabotage more or was it an organised attack in order to liberate parts of a territory? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it could be deemed sabotage rather than liberation of territory because they did not stay there. Perhaps they even left it during the course of a single day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 43 of today's transcript, lines 1 through 9, you said: "Deronjic told me that he was going to a meeting in Bratunac."

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: That's right, the command in Bratunac. Sorry I did not say the command in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we are in Bratunac and the command is in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You said that the meeting lasted only 30 minutes and that for the most part what was discussed was what would be done with the Muslims and that that was addressed to all the interlocutors at the meeting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And information about the 10.00 meeting, that it should be attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there another topic that remains in your memory that was raised during those 30 minutes?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it possible that Mr. Deronjic knew that he would not be able to attend that meeting and that that is why he delegated you, because you said that you did not understand why he had delegated you? Is there that possibility that he realised that he could not attend, that he wanted someone from the municipality to attend? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three of us from the municipality that came to that meeting. I personally think that Deronjic was trying to dodge that meeting because he, how should I put this, he did not have the fairest possible relations with General Mladic and I think he simply wanted to avoid coming to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you the ranking person from the municipality that attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody else is a senior person to me, the president of the municipality, I was president of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In terms of the responsibility for carrying out the tasks that were referred to here, so were these tasks and assignments first addressed to the president of the Assembly and only then to you as the executive organ who was supposed to carry this out?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my feeling was that we were all invited there as equals, no one was -- I am sorry. Well, the president of the municipality, and I as president of the Executive Board, and Aleksandar Tesic as head of the Ministry of Defence, and the local priest was in attendance as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you mentioned the head of the Ministry of Defence, in war time municipal departments of the Ministry of Defence, were they in the chain of command, and in terms of hierarchy, were they linked to the Ministry of Defence or municipal structures?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They carried out mobilisation and they were directly subordinated to the Ministry of Defence. Not to the civilian structures of the local municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was the civilian protection organ from that ministry also subordinated to them then as well?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I'm convinced that that is the case. The Ministry of Defence referred people to the civilian protection, not the Executive Board. The Ministry of Defence mobilised them and referred them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. When it comes to the military obligation, it could be work obligation or a military obligation. Was the work obligation under the authorities of the civilian protection or some municipal bodies? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work obligation was one and the same as the military obligation and the mobilisation was carried out by the Ministry of Defence. Which means that the two obligations are the same. They were equal. Work obligation was where people worked in companies, in institution, schools, health centres. And military obligation is in the military.

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let me try and rephrase. If you interrupted any actions that was performed by a gentleman who -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have to redact again a question, and you should be very careful with that otherwise we can't come to a conclusion. We have to redact page 80 line 25, through page 81, line 3. Please carry on. And if you want to put questions like these, we should go into private session before.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll try not to. We are coming to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would ask the witness this: Were you able to interrupt any action performed by the bodies of the civilian protection in the territory of your municipality pursuant to an order of the Ministry of Defence - thank you - or the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you issue a decision for them not to be engaged in those tasks?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't issue such a decision. Nobody ever asked me, nor was I in a position to render such a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you get involved in the cleanup of the front lines or the theatre of war in any way?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not of the front line, but of the town where women and children lived, yes, but not the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, on occasions you have told us something about the gentleman who was first in Zvornik and then in Banja Koviljaca and further on he underwent surgery, and so and so forth, and then he was found in one of the mass graves. How far was that from the location where your municipality was, where your municipal building was?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 50 to 55 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And how far was the place where he was treated the last time ever?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 60 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you remember that we have seen a document here where it says that he was admitted to a bigger hospital after having been discharged from Loznica?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, first he was admitted in Koviljaca and then at Loznica, but the distance between the two is about 5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you, at the time when war activities were taking place in that municipality where Kozluk was located, did you move without an approval of the military bodies?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I didn't have to. It was 55 kilometres away from me. What would I have been doing there in a foreign territory?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the -- witness, for the answers that you've provided here. I would like to thank you for your testimony. I apologise for the unpleasant questions that you had to answer, I wish you a pleasant journey, God bless you and my additional questions are now over.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank the Trial Chamber for having given me this opportunity to put additional question after the re-examination. I don't want to keep the witness any longer despite the fact that I have a lot more questions to ask him, I would like him to be able to go home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. Judge Mindua has a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, just a very short question, actually I just need a clarification. When you talked about Muslims who would run away from Bratunac and from Srebrenica --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving any interpretation yet again. Now it's better. I can hear you now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I was saying, it's just a clarification question. When we talked about Muslims who were running away from Bratunac and Srebrenica, you said yesterday on page 62, line 15 to 20 of the transcript and today on page 45, line 3 to 8 of the transcript, you mentioned today again that those Muslims did not want to surrender their weapons and they also did not want to surrender because their hands were bloody. Bloody from crimes committed by themselves, of course. Here is my question: Can you please tell us when you were mentioning these bloody crimes, what were you actually alluding to? Which crimes were you talking about, please tell us?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic used this term hands covered with blood or bloody hands, and I just quoted him. He said that those men whose hands were covered with blood would be prosecuted or processed. I don't know if I've made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well. But you do not know which crime these people would have committed? You personally do not know which crimes those are?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that the general meant constant incursions of the Muslim forces from the enclave into the Serbian villages where they committed crimes, where they killed people, where they looted and torched. I believe that that is what he meant. Many such crimes were committed by the Muslim side in Bratunac municipality. I've told you that probably 90 per cent of the Serbian villages in Bratunac and Srebrenica municipalities were torched and destroyed, and I believe that the general meant those people who had done that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Last question: Were these crimes committed in 1995, were these crimes committed in 1992 or even in 1993?

utterances.speaker: PW-063 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that the general meant all the crimes starting in 1992 through the entire period of war until about that time in 1995 when he said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir, you will be pleased to hear that this concludes your testimony and your examination. The Chamber would like to thank you for your attendance here in The Hague and for the answers you were able to provide. Now you are free to return to your normal activities. Thank you very much again. We have to adjourn and resume tomorrow in the morning 9.00 in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And please stay there until the Chamber has --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you, Your Honours, as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please wait until the Chamber has left the courtroom, witness. Are you on your feet to --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am actually, I'll only be a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... rising because we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just wanted to, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, refer you to the discussion that we had preliminarily concerning a witness. I just wanted to let you know that that person is a witness in this case. That person is, for the record, I think it's okay, is PW-066. And you will find the references to the matters that we addressed in the associated evidence, it's a 92 bis witness. In addition, I would let you know also that we do have additional documents that were issued by the chief of public security, Dragomir Vasic, for the 12th of July, 1995. There were about four or five of them and we can make those available to the Trial Chamber too by way of a bar table motion since it was alluded to in this case. The urgent document that is in evidence was a daily report. And that's essentially it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For this information. We adjourn now and resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of October, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
